subject: Interop benchmark plan and next steps — ACME AI PoC
messages:
From: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan@acme.ai>, Priya Shah <priya@acme.ai>
Cc: sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 1 Sep 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Interop benchmark plan and next steps — ACME AI PoC

Hi Jordan / Priya —

Thanks for the demo earlier — great discussion. I wanted to capture the agreed scope and proposed next steps so we keep momentum. TL;DR below, details after.

TL;DR
- Redwood will run a short interoperability benchmark vs ACME's current hyperscaler baseline and validate an OpenAI-API-compatible surface for your top prompts.
- Proposed tests: latency tail + throughput, prompt/response fidelity (top 50 prompts), and an SDK swap smoke test in your dev environment.
- Proposed owners: Redwood (Sergio lead), ACME (Priya lead). Target technical deep-dive week of Sep 7; please confirm availability.

Recap & goals
- Your primary success criteria: match or improve 95th/99th latency, keep per-token accuracy within acceptable diffs on critical prompts, and a frictionless SDK swap for devs.
- Secondary: deployment isolation, predictable unit cost, and transparent fallbacks.

Differentiators to validate in PoC (what we'll demonstrate)
1) Production-first runtime: continuous batching + prefix caching to keep p95 low under bursty traffic.
2) OpenAI-compatible surface: minimal code changes for SDKs and same chat/completions semantics in most cases.
3) Cost controls: batching/quantization knobs and per-route cost visibility.

Proposed tests (short descriptions)
A. Latency & throughput benchmark (owner: Redwood / Sergio)
- Run p50/p95/p99 vs your recorded baseline (same model family + token lengths).
- Measure cold vs hot cache, KV-cache hit rates, and throughput under synthetic concurrency.
B. Prompt fidelity (owner: ACME + Redwood)
- Take top 50 production prompts (we'll help with sampling) and run them against your hyperscaler baseline and Redwood.
- Record tokenization diffs, token counts, top-level text diffs, and a simple scoring pass on business-critical QA.
C. SDK swap smoke test (owner: ACME dev + Redwood SE)
- Swap one dev service to Redwood's OpenAI-compatible SDK (single endpoint change).
- Verify CI run and basic e2e behavior.

Deliverables
- Benchmark report (p50/p95/p99, throughput)
- Prompt diff matrix + sample golden/failed cases
- SDK swap playbook + sample code snippet

Attachments: ACME-redwood-poc-checklist.pdf (short checklist) and interop-bench-config.yaml (bench config).

Commercial ask
- Please confirm whether we should produce a 3-month dedicated capacity quote for billing/commit modeling (helps prioritize capacity reservation).

Next steps
- Priya to confirm technical attendees and provide sample prompt set (top 50) by Sep 3.
- We propose a 90-minute technical deep dive week of Sep 7–10; Sergio will own the runbook.
- Rafael will coordinate the commercial sketch once we have rough capacity needs.

Thanks — excited to run the tests and show the measurable deltas.

Best,
Rafael Mendes
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Thanks, Rafael — useful summary. A few clarifications from our side before we lock dates: 

1) Compliance: ACME handles PHI for a subset of customers — can Redwood support HIPAA workflows and sign a BA? We need to understand any gaps (SOC 2 + HIPAA required).
2) Data residency: primary workloads must stay in US-EAST region; please confirm your hosting options.
3) OpenAI compatibility: we need to know whether any behavioral diffs are expected out of the box (tokenization/newline handling). If you expect diffs, what mitigations do you recommend?
4) Commercial: can you give a ballpark for a 3-month dedicated reservation (GPU hours or monthly commit) so legal can budget?

We can get the top-50 prompt export to you by EOD Sep 3. Assuming you have HIPAA cover and US-EAST options, Priya and I can do the 90-min deep dive on Sep 8 (10:00 AM PT).

-Jordan
Jordan Blake
Head of Platform Engineering, ACME AI
jordan@acme.ai

From: Sergio Alvarez <sergio.alvarez@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan@acme.ai>, Priya Shah <priya@acme.ai>
Cc: Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.ai>, marissa.cole@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 2 Sep 2026 09:31:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Interop benchmark plan and next steps — ACME AI PoC

Jordan — thanks for the quick questions. Short answers + proposed mitigations below.

Compliance & residency
- Redwood supports SOC 2 Type II; we have a HIPAA addendum and customer BA template for covered workflows. I'll loop security for a formal checklist if ACME wants to proceed with PHI in the PoC.
- We can pin the PoC to us-east-1 (dedicated/private deployment) — I'll include region config in the interop-bench-config.yaml attachment.

OpenAI compatibility and prompt diffs
- We expose an OpenAI-compatible surface (same endpoints and parameter names) but there are a few places prompts can diverge: tokenizer variants (affects token counts), whitespace/newline normalization, and some temperature/stop-sequence edge cases.
- Expected impact: for ~90% of prompts you'll see bit-for-bit parity on model families we validate; the remaining 10% are often caused by leading/trailing whitespace or tokenizer splits.
- Mitigations: prompt canonicalization script (we'll provide a small utility) and a short golden-case test harness to detect regressions. We'll include the script example in the drive link.

Latency guidance (expected)
- For the model family we discussed, typical p95 on Redwood Dedicated in us-east under identical sequence lengths is within 5–15% of the hyperscaler baseline, with lower unit cost due to batching. We'll validate exact numbers during the benchmark run.

Commercial sketch
- For a 3-month reserved pool sized for your projected dev/test concurrency, a rough ballpark is $XXk–$YYk/month (high-level estimate). Rafael will produce a formal quote once you confirm target QPS and model family.

Proposed next actions
- Priya: please upload the top-50 prompt set by EOD Sep 3 (S3 link or shared Drive).
- Rafael: schedule the 90-min deep dive on Sep 8 10:00 AM PT (accept calendar).
- Sergio (Redwood): run an initial lab benchmark and share config + results within 48 hours of receiving prompt set.

Attachments: interop-bench-config.yaml (bench knobs + region).

--
Sergio Alvarez
Principal Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
